claimBlocks.text: San Carlos Apache College’s2025–26catalog traces its charter to2014 and opening to August2017. Its stated goals connect higher education with language and cultural renewal. Introductory language courses emphasize speaking, reading and listening, followed by grammar and increasingly complex communication. These are a particular college’s institutional history and planned curriculum, rather than proof of current enrolment, fluency outcomes or one language program for every Apache people.

claimBlocks.suggestedSection: Families and educators shaping early learning
claimBlocks.text: A2025Extension report describes Gowa as a San Carlos partnership involving tribal officials, schools, a library and early-childhood services. San Carlos Apache educator Melody Grace Thomas explains selecting books with Indigenous authors, people and settings while working with Apache Language Preservation. The account shows local participation in educational materials. It does not independently establish the program’s effects or imply identical family practices across Apache communities.

claimBlocks.suggestedSection: Reading language statistics with their limits
claimBlocks.text: The2024White Mountain regional report brings together census-based home-language categories, school language records and a Head Start questionnaire. Those sources ask different questions of different groups, so their results are not interchangeable measures of Apache fluency. Its language-program discussion draws on an earlier2022report. This makes the publication useful for understanding evidence and local context, while leaving present language use and individual learning outcomes to further research.
